title: Gateway: Intent-based Admin Provisioning & Escalation Playbook
creator: Priya Patel
description: Create an intent-driven intake and escalation playbook that standardizes how enterprise admin/access requests (RBAC role grants, SSO/SAML onboarding, SCIM provisioning changes, org policy exceptions) are classified, prioritized, and routed. The playbook is intended for PM/Support/SEs and will power UI intake forms, an operator runbook, and a first-pass automated scorer used by the Access Concierge service.
summary: Customers and internal teams currently submit admin and access requests through multiple channels (support tickets, account teams, partner forms). This ticket consolidates decision logic, SLAs, routing, and escalation paths into a single 'Gateway' playbook and delivery plan. Deliverables: intake schema, priority scoring rubric, routing matrix, escalation SLA table, operator runbook, and rollout checklist.
tasks: Audit historical admin/access tickets and categorize by outcome and time-to-resolution
Design minimal intake schema (intent, scope, sensitivity, org size, requested TTL) usable by UI and API
Define priority scoring (risk-weighted factors: data access, production impact, legal/regulatory)
Map routing rules to teams and channels (Support -> Concierge -> Platform Ops -> Security)
Draft on-call escalation paths and SLA targets for P0/P1/P2 admin requests
Prototype a lightweight automated scorer (rules + weights) for first-pass triage
Write operator runbook with rollback, auditing, and post-mortem templates
Coordinate security review and legal sign-off for high-sensitivity flows
acceptance_criteria: Intake schema committed to the spec repo and used by at least one intake UI prototype
Priority scoring rubric documented with example request classifications and expected SLA
Routing matrix implemented in the support triage handbook and validated with 3 sample requests
Operator runbook reviewed and signed by Platform Ops and Security
Automated scorer prototype reduces manual misroute rate by >=40% on a 90-day historical sample
comments: 2026-02-23 - Priya Patel: Kickoff meeting notes added. Initial hypothesis: many requests are misclassified because intent fields are missing. Action: run ticket taxonomy sweep.

2026-02-28 - Connor Li: Pulled 180 days of support tickets; created spreadsheet with preliminary buckets (SSO onboarding, role grant, SCIM mapping, policy exception). Observed 22% of requests lacked org context.

2026-03-02 - Asha Mehta: Design constraints — intake must fit inside a 3-field quick flow for self-serve customers; full form for enterprise support. Mockups in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Admin+Gateway+Mockups
2026-03-04 - Security (Diego Alvarez): Raised sensitivity for custom role grants; recommended additional attestation and audit log requirements. Marked flow as 'requires security gating'.
2026-03-07 - Connor Li: Built initial scoring rules in a spreadsheet; sample rules reduced ambiguous routing from 28% -> 12% on 30-day sample. Next: build proto scorer service.
2026-03-09 - Legal (Marta Kovács): Noted cross-border SCIM mappings require data residency checks for some EMEA customers; added dependency for policy enforcement in Private deployments.
2026-03-10 - Priya Patel: Decided to split rollout into two phases: (1) internal-only Gateway for Support + SEs, (2) gradual self-serve rollout with UI constraints. Added to rollout checklist.
risks: Automated scoring may under-classify high-risk requests without adequate attestation fields
Cross-team coordination (Support, Security, Platform Ops) could delay SLAs
Self-serve UI may collect insufficient context leading to re-opened tickets
mitigations: Pivot to conservative routing for ambiguous scores (route to Security review queue)
Schedule weekly syncs with Platform Ops and Security until M2 rollout
Enforce minimal required fields for self-serve and provide inline help to reduce missing context
